input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 6 gives a convenience right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding" — i.e. exactly when no work is being performed. While any engagement is live we have no convenience exit at all (only breach termination under 6(b)), and there is no refund of prepaid fees, so the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback Customer-side elements. The same gating condition works in our favour on the Vendor side: Contractor cannot walk away while a Statement of Work is outstanding, so the "no Vendor convenience right during a committed term" element is already met and we have not disturbed it. We therefore add a Company-only right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, leaving the mutual 15-day right in 6(a) intact.

proposal.summary: Add a Company-only convenience termination right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Today we may only walk away for convenience when no Statement of Work is outstanding, which locks us in for the life of every engagement. We have added a Company-only right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Contractor's convenience right remains limited to periods with no outstanding Statement of Work.

ops.text: In addition, Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees on a pro rata basis for the period after the effective date of such termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
